headline: Crab processor closes after forty years, and the boats have nowhere else to land
standfirst: The nearest alternative buyer is a hundred and ten miles by road, which is further than the margin will stretch.

image.alt: Stacked crab pots on a quayside

body.text: Thirty-one jobs go at the end of the month, and around fourteen boats lose their only local market. The company cited energy costs and a collapse in the Asian export price, in that order.
Skippers are already talking about switching to live export, which pays better per kilo but requires vivier transport and a buyer prepared to take small, irregular loads. Nobody has found one yet.
